findings.issue: The --extend warning says 'Pass --convergence-mode=off or use stopPolicy max-iterations to keep it running.' Neither works on an extended run. step_extend_completed_run rewrites only status, maxIterations, maxDurationMinutes, lineageMode and continuedFromRun in the config. It never writes antiConvergence.convergenceMode or stopPolicy. The only writer of those keys is step_create_config (lines 880 and 888), which runs for a new session only. On every iteration the loop reads convergence_mode and stop_policy back from deep-review-config.json (lines 1177-1178) and passes that value to convergence.cjs as --convergence-mode (line 1245). A --convergence-mode=off flag given with --extend therefore never reaches the stop decision. The reader also cannot set stopPolicy by hand, because line 2612 forbids changing the config outside its writer steps and the template marks the config immutable. An extended run that follows this advice still re-stops on all_dimensions_clean. The fix is either to have the extension step persist those two flags into the config, or to change the advice to something that works.

evidence.out:
579: const stopPolicy = config.stopPolicy || "convergence";
583: ? "This run stops on convergence, ... Pass --convergence-mode=off or use stopPolicy max-iterations to keep it running."
880: antiConvergence.convergenceMode: "{convergence_mode}"
888: stopPolicy: "{stop_policy}"
1177: - stop_policy: "Extract stopPolicy from deep-review-config.json, default 'convergence'. ..."
1178: - convergence_mode: "Extract antiConvergence.convergenceMode ..."

findings.issue: The review_dimensions binding says it is the set of 'Dimensions to check' and that 'any other name is a custom dimension, reviewed after the canonical four in configured order', with no fan-out exception. Under fan-out that is not what happens. step_fanout_spawn_cli passes no dimensions to fanout-run.cjs, and fanout-run.cjs hard-codes 'review_dimensions: all' into the setup bindings of every lineage, both the CLI prompt and the native PRE-BOUND SETUP ANSWERS. A configured subset or a custom name is dropped without notice, and every lineage reviews only the canonical four. The doc needs to state that fan-out reviews only the canonical four, or the code needs to forward the configured dimensions.

Q_dims says 'Or add custom names after them (e.g., "correctness, performance"); a custom dimension is reviewed after the canonical four'. The review_dimensions row (line 72) and the YAML block (line 35) give no fan-out exception either. With two or more lineages (config.fanout), fanout-run.cjs binds 'review_dimensions: all' for every lineage, so both a subset answer and a custom name are discarded and no custom dimension is reviewed. The fan-out caveat is missing.

The maxIterations row gives the expansive resize as 'min(24, max(7, 2·c·(S + maxDepth − 1)))' with 'c the four canonical dimensions plus any custom name' and says the budget is 'kept at 7 when S is 0'. That describes the single-executor run only. A fan-out lineage with no matrix iterations value is sized by expansiveLineageBudgets in fanout-run.cjs (lines 339-352) from its own seed share, with c fixed at 4. Its floor and zero-share budget is 12 for a native lineage and 7 only for a CLI one. The row should name the fan-out lineage budget or limit itself to a single run.
